modules.title: Retail Trade
modules.html:
Meaning

Home (internal/domestic) trade is buying and selling within the boundaries of one country. It has two branches: retail and wholesale trade.

A retailer is the last link in the chain of distribution, breaking bulk and selling in small quantities to the final consumer.

Types of Retailers

  1. Small-scale retailers – hawkers, pedlars, street traders, market stall holders, mobile shops, kiosks, unit/single shops.
  2. Large-scale retailers – department stores, multiple (chain) shops, supermarkets, hypermarkets, mail-order houses, co-operative retail societies, discount houses and e-commerce stores.

Functions of the Retailer

  • Breaks bulk and sells in convenient quantities.
  • Holds a variety of goods near consumers, saving them travel.
  • Grants credit and sometimes hire purchase facilities.
  • Offers after-sales service, delivery and advice.
  • Passes consumer opinion back to wholesalers and manufacturers.

Comparing Large-Scale Retail Organisations

TypeKey featureWeakness
Department storeMany departments under one roof, central controlVery high overheads
Multiple shopBranches selling a narrow range of similar goodsInflexible, no credit
SupermarketSelf-service, low prices, fast turnoverShoplifting; impulse buying
Mail orderSells by catalogue/post; no shop neededGoods not inspected before purchase

examples.q: A supermarket buys cartons of milk at ₦4,800 each and sells at ₦6,000. Calculate the mark-up and the margin.
State three reasons why small-scale retailers survive in Nigeria despite competition from supermarkets.
examples.a: They are located within neighbourhoods and open long hours; they grant informal credit to known customers; they sell in very small (broken) units such as a cup of rice or a sachet of detergent that large stores do not offer.

modules.title: Wholesale Trade and Middlemen
modules.html:
The Wholesaler

A wholesaler buys in large quantities from manufacturers and sells in smaller lots to retailers. Types include general merchants, specialist wholesalers, cash-and-carry wholesalers, rack jobbers and merchant/agent middlemen (brokers, factors, del credere agents).

Services to the Manufacturer

  • Buys in bulk, freeing factory storage space.
  • Provides finance by prompt payment.
  • Bears the risk of price fall, deterioration and bad debts.
  • Supplies market information and sometimes handles packaging and branding.
  • Reduces the number of transactions the producer must handle.

Services to the Retailer

  • Breaks bulk into retail-size lots.
  • Grants trade credit and trade discount.
  • Delivers goods and holds stock on the retailer's behalf.
  • Advises on new products and grants preparation of goods (grading, blending, packing).

Chain of Distribution

Producer → Wholesaler → Retailer → Consumer. It may be shortened where producers sell directly (factory shops, e-commerce, industrial goods) or lengthened by the use of agents.

Can Middlemen Be Eliminated?

The middleman may be by-passed, but his functions – breaking bulk, storage, finance, risk-bearing, transport – cannot disappear; someone must perform them, and the cost remains.

examples.q: A wholesaler buys 500 bags of cement at ₦8,000 each, receives 12.5% trade discount, and sells all at ₦8,600 each. Find his profit.
Explain the difference between a broker and a del credere agent.
examples.a: A broker merely brings buyer and seller together for a commission (brokerage) and never takes possession of goods or guarantees payment. A del credere agent sells on behalf of the principal and, for an extra commission, guarantees payment by the buyer, thus bearing the bad-debt risk.

modules.title: Documents and Terms of Home Trade
modules.html:
Sequence of Documents

  1. Letter of enquiry – buyer asks about goods, price and terms.
  2. Quotation / price list / catalogue – seller's reply.
  3. Order (purchase order) – buyer formally requests goods.
  4. Advice note – tells the buyer goods have been dispatched.
  5. Delivery note – accompanies the goods; signed on receipt.
  6. Invoice – the bill; shows quantity, price, discounts and total amount payable.
  7. Debit note – corrects an undercharge on an invoice.
  8. Credit note – corrects an overcharge or covers returns (printed in red).
  9. Statement of account – monthly summary of transactions and balance due.
  10. Receipt – acknowledges payment.

Common Abbreviations

TermMeaning
E. & O.E.Errors and omissions excepted
C.O.D.Cash on delivery
C.W.O.Cash with order
Carriage paidSeller bears transport cost
Pro-forma invoiceInvoice sent before sale/goods on approval

Discounts

  • Trade discount – deduction from list price given by one trader to another; it is the retailer's profit margin.
  • Cash discount – deduction for prompt payment, e.g. “5% 7 days, net 30”.
  • Quantity discount – for buying in large volume.

Turnover and Rate of Stock Turn

$$\text{Rate of Stock Turn} = \dfrac{\text{Cost of Goods Sold}}{\text{Average Stock at Cost}}$$

where \( \text{Average Stock} = \dfrac{\text{Opening Stock} + \text{Closing Stock}}{2} \).

examples.q: Goods listed at ₦200,000 are sold at 15% trade discount with terms 5% cash discount for payment within 7 days. How much is paid if the buyer settles on the 5th day?
Opening stock ₦120,000, closing stock ₦80,000, cost of goods sold ₦600,000. Find the rate of stock turn and interpret it.
examples.a: Average stock \(=\dfrac{120{,}000+80{,}000}{2}=₦100{,}000\). Rate of stock turn \(=\dfrac{600{,}000}{100{,}000}=6\) times a year, i.e. the shop clears and replaces its stock every two months – a healthy turnover for general goods.

Retail trade: types of retailers and their functions is a key part of Home Trade (SSS 1, Commerce). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Meaning Home (internal/domestic) trade is buying and selling within the boundaries of one country.
  • It has two branches: retail and wholesale trade.
  • A retailer is the last link in the chain of distribution, breaking bulk and selling in small quantities to the final consumer.
  • Types of Retailers Small-scale retailers – hawkers, pedlars, street traders, market stall holders, mobile shops, kiosks, unit/single shops.
  • Large-scale retailers – department stores, multiple (chain) shops, supermarkets, hypermarkets, mail-order houses, co-operative retail societies, discount houses and e-commerce stores.

Worked example

Q: Home trade is trade carried on
A: Within a country — Home trade takes place within the boundaries of one country.

Q: Trade discount is given
A: By one trader to another off the list price — Trade discount is a deduction from catalogue price between traders; it forms the retailer's margin.

quiz.q: Home trade is trade carried on
quiz.solution: Home trade takes place within the boundaries of one country.

quiz.q: The last link in the chain of distribution is the
quiz.solution: The retailer sells directly to the final consumer.

quiz.q: A document that corrects an overcharge on an invoice is a
quiz.solution: A credit note reduces the amount owed – used for overcharges and returns.

quiz.q: Trade discount is given
options: By one trader to another off the list price
quiz.solution: Trade discount is a deduction from catalogue price between traders; it forms the retailer's margin.

quiz.q: E. & O.E. on an invoice means
quiz.solution: It reserves the seller's right to correct clerical mistakes later.

quiz.q: A wholesaler serves the manufacturer mainly by
options: Buying in bulk and providing finance
quiz.solution: Bulk buying frees factory space and prompt payment finances further production.

quiz.q: Which retail organisation uses catalogues and the post?
quiz.solution: Mail-order houses sell by catalogue and deliver by post/courier.

quiz.q: Self-service is the main feature of a
quiz.solution: Customers pick goods themselves and pay at the checkout.

quiz.q: If cost is ₦800 and selling price ₦1,000, the margin is
quiz.solution: Margin = profit/selling price = 200/1000 = 20%.

quiz.q: Using the same figures, the mark-up is
quiz.solution: Mark-up = profit/cost = 200/800 = 25%.

quiz.q: The document that accompanies goods and is signed by the buyer is the
quiz.solution: The delivery note travels with the goods and is signed as proof of receipt.

quiz.q: Rate of stock turn is cost of goods sold divided by
quiz.solution: Average stock at cost is the denominator.

quiz.q: An agent who guarantees payment by the buyer is a
quiz.solution: For an extra commission the del credere agent bears the bad-debt risk.

quiz.q: A pro-forma invoice is sent
quiz.solution: It is used for goods on approval, cash-with-order sales or as a quotation.

quiz.q: Middlemen can best be described as
options: Performers of functions that cannot be eliminated
quiz.solution: You may by-pass the middleman but not his functions of bulk-breaking, storage, finance and risk-bearing.

quiz.q: C.O.D. in trade means
quiz.solution: The buyer pays cash when the goods are delivered.

quiz.q: Home trade consists of...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Wholesale and Retail trade.

quiz.q: Home Trade:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Within country.

quiz.q: Trade credit allows a buyer to?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Pay later.

quiz.q: Wholesale trade helps?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Bridge the gap.

quiz.q: Which of the following describes 'invisible trade'?
options: Trade in services such as tourism
quiz.solution: Invisible trade refers to the import and export of services, where no physical goods are moved across borders.

quiz.q: The act of selling goods in foreign markets at prices lower than those in the home market is _____.
quiz.solution: Dumping is a predatory pricing strategy used to gain market share in another country, often resulting in unfair competition.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a type of internal trade?
quiz.solution: Wholesale trade happens within the boundaries of a single country, making it a form of home/internal trade.

quiz.q: A trade where goods are imported and then re-exported to another country is _____.
quiz.solution: Entrepôt trade involves importing goods from one country for the purpose of exporting them to another.

quiz.q: The term 'f.o.b' in international trade stands for _____.
quiz.solution: Free on board means the seller's responsibility ends once the goods are loaded onto the ship.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a barrier to international trade?
quiz.solution: Language barriers can make communication and negotiations difficult between traders from different countries.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an auxiliary to trade?
quiz.solution: Insurance is an aid to trade because it helps manage the risks involved in business activities.

quiz.q: The process of buying and selling goods within the boundaries of a single country is _____ trade.
quiz.solution: Home or internal trade occurs within a specific nation, involving wholesalers and retailers.

quiz.q: The term 'entrepot' trade refers to _____.
options: selling goods on the high seas
quiz.solution: Entrepot trade involves importing goods from one country and exporting them to another without significant processing.

quiz.q: Which document is required when goods are to be exported to a country with which the exporter's country has a trade agreement?
quiz.solution: A Certificate of Origin proves the country where goods were manufactured, often used to qualify for lower tariffs.

quiz.q: The act of selling goods in a foreign market at a price lower than the cost of production or the price in the home market is _____.
quiz.solution: Dumping is a predatory pricing strategy used to gain market share in another country, often seen as unfair competition.

quiz.q: Entrepot trade involves:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Re-exporting imported goods.

quiz.q: Visible trade involves:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Goods/Merchandise.

quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Manufacturing.

quiz.q: Trade between countries is called:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: International trade.

quiz.q: The practice of selling goods abroad at a lower price than at home is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Dumping.

quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Insurance.

quiz.q: Entrepot trade:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Re-exporting imported goods.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an aid-to-trade?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Warehousing.

quiz.q: International trade involves the exchange of goods between...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Two or more countries.

quiz.q: Visible trade refers to the import and export of...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Tangible/Physical goods.

quiz.q: Entrepot trade is...
options: Importing goods for the purpose of re-exporting them
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Importing goods for the purpose of re-exporting them.
